## Summary

The May and November 2026 [[stripe]] guides describe how Radar evaluates hundreds of network and payment risk factors to assign a risk score and level and decide when to block a payment or mark it for review. Merchants can inspect those signals through **Show all insights** on a payment. Both guides state that Stripe retains Risk Insights data for up to six months and that the interface is unavailable for older transactions.

## Customer Signals

Risk Insights can show cardholder name and email correspondence, the Stripe network authorization rate associated with that email, and billing, shipping and IP locations. A low authorization rate might indicate suspicious behavior. Integration-provided details such as cardholder email, IP address and shipping address help Radar compute the data used in its assessment. See the [[source-stripe-radar-optimize-risk-factors|integration checklist]] for the data inputs.

## Fraud Factor Detail in the 2026-05-10 Guide

The May guide describes Risk Insights as available with Radar for Fraud Teams. Its section on fraud factor numbers and **Top Fraud Factors** describes data for charges made within the previous six months, with sandbox payments outside that feature’s scope.

- **Fraud factor numbers** compare the likelihood of fraud for charges with similar values for a factor against the Stripe average. A 3.5× factor means charges with similar values for that factor are 3.5 times as likely to be fraudulent as the Stripe average. May expects some factors above 1 for higher-risk payments and some below 1 for lower-risk payments. Hover details show the distribution of possible values, which can change over time.
- **Top Fraud Factors** highlights values commonly associated with fraud. Radar can identify a fraud pattern from multiple factors even if none looks suspicious individually.

November retains **Show all insights** and the six-month interface restriction. It omits the May plan label, fraud factor number and Top Fraud Factors explanations, and sandbox wording. Eligibility for those details under the newer plans and in sandboxes remains unresolved in these captures.

## Related Payments

Both dedicated Risk Insights captures describe other payments to the merchant’s own business that share the viewed payment’s customer ID, IP address, or card number. Many cards using one IP or multiple customers sharing a card can help investigate patterns such as card testing or trial abuse.

> **2026-11-07 documentation difference.** The dedicated Risk Insights guide lists customer ID, IP address, or card number. The same-day [[raw/stripe-radar-transaction-reviews-2026-11-07|Transaction Reviews guide]] (line 52) lists email address, IP address, or card number for its Related Payments link. The captures leave the reason for the identifier difference and the actual lookup behavior unresolved.

radar-reviews-risk-insights.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/reviews/risk-insights, source-stripe-radar-risk-insights retains the May 10 detail and adds the November 7 full capture. Both describe Radar evaluating hundreds of factors to score/level a payment and use those results to decide whether to block or mark it for review. A merchant can open Show all insights, and transactions older than the up-to-six-month retention window cannot use the interface (old raw lines 8-13, old raw lines 23-28, new raw lines 9-16). The integrator provides signal values such as email, IP and shipping address to support fuller assessment. The merchant may inspect name/email correspondence, network authorization rate associated with email, billing/shipping/IP geography, and other payments to its own business sharing customer ID, IP or card number. A low authorization rate might indicate suspicious behavior, and common links can help investigate card testing or trial abuse. Neither is an automatic fraud verdict (old raw lines 15-21, old raw lines 51-56, new raw lines 18-28). The revised summary dates the Fraud Teams and sandbox statements to May and presents the authorization rate as a possible signal. November retains the interface guidance and leaves the availability of the detailed factors under newer plans and in sandboxes unresolved (old raw lines 8-21, old raw lines 30-49, new raw lines 9-24).
radar-reviews-risk-insights.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/reviews/risk-insights, source-stripe-radar-risk-insights retains the May guide and adds the full November guide. May 10 documents Risk Insights with Fraud Teams and gives fraud-factor and Top Fraud Factors detail, a charge window of six months and no sandbox support for the feature in that section. Its ratios are comparisons against an average, and directional high/low factor descriptions are expectations. November 7 omits those details but retains Show all insights and up to six months of interface access. This documentary reduction does not establish feature removal, broadened access or changed sandbox availability (old raw lines 8-13, old raw lines 23-49, new raw lines 9-24). Moving Show all insights, replacing screenshots and changing Review from radar/reviews to radar/transaction-reviews are presentation or navigation (old raw lines 23-28, old raw lines 51-61, new raw lines 9-14, new raw lines 26-36). Preserve the dedicated Related Payments customer ID/IP/card wording from both captures. The separate November Review guide raw/stripe-radar-transaction-reviews-2026-11-07.md at line 52 says email/IP/card instead. The source preserves the two documented descriptions and leaves actual lookup behavior unresolved (old raw lines 51-56, new raw lines 26-31). The revised source and proposed concept changes preserve the reciprocal stripe-radar route, dated eligibility and sandbox scope, and the transaction review and integration checklist routes.

## Risk Insights (Fraud Teams)

Explains why Radar scored a payment. Available for last 6 months only; not in sandbox. Shows: fraud factor numbers (multiplier vs Stripe average, e.g. 3.5x), top fraud factors, customer signals (name/email match, email auth rate on network), geography (billing/shipping/IP), and related payments (same IP/card — detect card testing and trial abuse). See [[source-stripe-radar-risk-insights]].
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown:
## Risk Insights

The May and November 2026 guides describe payment-level risk signals, **Show all insights**, and up to six months of data and interface access. The May guide names Fraud Teams and documents fraud factor multipliers, Top Fraud Factors, and a sandbox restriction in its fraud-factor section. November omits those details. See [[source-stripe-radar-risk-insights]] for the dated scope, customer and geography signals, and the comparison method.

The dedicated guides describe Related Payments by customer ID, IP address, or card number. The separate November [[source-stripe-radar-reviews|Transaction Reviews guide]] describes email address, IP address, or card number. The difference between the documented identifiers remains unresolved.
